createdBy: code review R8, agent A (measured and expanded by the implementer)
impact: All three .trim() sites remain unfixed in the shipped CLI (src/ccusage.ts:40-41, src/runner.ts:276), so the five measured divergences vs usage.py:118 stand; the reachable trigger is a BOM-only stream (which ALLOWLIST 12 deliberately preserves), which flips the frozen error branch and, in the stderr cases, changes the message body itself. Confined to error paths — no success-path output is affected — and the fix is mechanical: one pyStrip built from the PY_WHITESPACE set already defined at src/context.ts:78, applied at all three sites together.
resolution:
All three sites moved to a Python-faithful strip, together, as the issue required.

NEW: src/pystr.ts — a leaf module holding Python's whitespace set once, with PY_WHITESPACE (the str.split() separator) and pyStrip (str.strip()) generated from a single character class. CPython routes both through Py_UNICODE_ISSPACE, so one set genuinely serves both; verified by enumerating U+0000-U+10FFF and finding no code point where `c.strip()==""` and `c.split()==[]` disagree. Generating both regexes from one class matters for the same reason T-005 collapsed the parity matrix: two spellings of one set drift silently.

CALL SITES:
- src/ccusage.ts:41-42 — `res.stdout.trim()` and `res.stderr.trim()` -> pyStrip. These are usage.py:119-120, where strip both selects the failure branch and supplies the message body.
- src/runner.ts:276 — `stdout.trim()` -> pyStrip; the comment saying `.trim()` was deliberate "because fixing it here alone would split the decision" is now obsolete and was rewritten.
- src/context.ts — PY_WHITESPACE moved out to pystr.ts; splitCommand imports it. No behavior change, one definition.
- Swept src/: no `.trim()` remains anywhere in shipping code.

MEASURED SET DIFFERENCE (29 Python vs 25 JS, differing in both directions):
- Python only: U+001C-U+001F, U+0085
- JS only: U+FEFF

TESTS — differential against live CPython, in unicode-parity.test.mjs's existing style (ENOENT skips; an oracle that ran and failed is a hard error, never a silent skip):
1. pyStrip vs str.strip() over a corpus placing every character of the union in every position.
2. splitCommand vs str.split() over the same corpus.
3. The disagreement is pinned as exactly those six code points, in both directions — a reversion to .trim() cannot pass, nor can a hand-edited class that drops or invents a member.
4. The frozen decision end-to-end: nine (stdout, stderr, rc) triples run through runCcusage and compared against CPython evaluating usage.py:119-120's actual expressions. Covers both divergence directions, agreement controls, and rc=0 to guard the `and` rather than only the strip.
5. runner.test.mjs — the blank-stdout guard's own whitespace coverage.

MUTATION-VERIFIED (this is what caught the real gap):
- Revert ccusage.ts to .trim() -> branch test fails.
- Revert the whitespace class (drop U+001C) -> 4 tests fail.
- Revert runner.ts to .trim() -> INITIALLY PASSED ALL 318 TESTS. The runner's guard had no coverage distinguishing the two whitespace sets, so test 5 above was added specifically to close that; the reversion now fails it. Without mutation testing this fix would have shipped half-guarded.

Suite: 319 unit tests (was 314), contract 19/19, parity --final 266 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped, 45/45 goldens byte-match, test:all exit 0.
title: ccusage.ts uses JS .trim() where Python uses str.strip(): 5 measured message divergences
